title: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Feature Analysis in Vision Models
abstract: Modern Artificial Intelligence models have achieved strong performances across a wide range of downstream tasks, yet their inner workings still remain opaque to humans. One reason is superposition, whereby a single neuron may respond to several unrelated concepts simultaneously, which makes the model's internal computations difficult to inspect. Mechanistic interpretability is a research discipline that aims to resolve this problem, and recent works in this field have demonstrated that sparse autoencoders (SAE) can be a potential solution. However, applications of SAEs are limited to Transformer-based language models, and applications to vision models are still fairly understudied. Therefore, this thesis aims to evaluate the use of sparse autoencoders as a tool for mechanistic interpretability in vision models. For this purpose, the thesis first reviews existing literature that motivates this topic, then covers how sparse autoencoders have been used to disentangle neurons into individual features, and how these features have been used for causal steering in language and vision models. Building on this review, the thesis reports an experiment that examines whether the standard framework applies to an image tokenizer. The experiment trains a sparse autoencoder on UniTok, an image tokenizer that is capable of both image generation and semantic understanding. Through the experiment, this thesis seeks to determine whether SAE-based interpretability methods established in prior literature can generalize beyond the setting in which they were originally demonstrated.

title: Blockchain-Enabled Quantum-Auto GAN Framework for Secure and Robust Lung Cancer Diagnosis
abstract: Medical image diagnosis has evolved to become a vital resource in contemporary healthcare, facilitating early diagnosis and treatment of life-threatening diseases like lung cancer.Secure Medical Image Diagnosis aims at the creation of frameworks that not only provide high diagnostic accuracy but also maintain patient privacy and integrity of data.Current models suffer from several limitations, such as over fitting from small annotated datasets, elevated computational complexity of quantum-based models, inefficiencies in blockchain consensus algorithms, and privacy risk when handling sensitive medical images.To address these limitations, this work introduces an innovative integrated framework that brings together a hybrid Quantum-Auto GAN model and blockchain technology (Q-AGAN-BT).The Q-AGAN-BT carries out latent feature extraction, synthetic image generation, and quantum-boosted classification to enhance diagnostic accuracy and robustness, and blockchain provides safe storage, privacy protection in the form of encrypted off-chain data, access control based on smart contracts, and an innovative Proof of Medical Consensus (PoMC) for light-weight clinically authenticated validation.The novelty of this work is in presenting a very accurate, privacy-enabled, and tamper-resistant lung cancer diagnosis system that overcomes the drawbacks of current approaches and improves reliability and trustfulness in medical image handling.The Q-AGAN-BT model attained the best performance with 95.6% accuracy, 95.0%F1-score, and 0.98 AUC, surpassing classical and hybrid models like CNN + LSTM, Autoencoder + GAN, ResNet50, DenseNet121, and VGG16.The blockchain part provided secure and effective data handling with 0.12 s per-image encryption time, 0.03 s hash validation, 0.08 s smart contract delay, 85% storage savings, and 0.15 s PoMC verification per block, providing high diagnostic performance as well as strong and tamper-proof medical data processing.

title: Knowledge-Guided Temporal Fuzzy Learning for Interpretable Prediction of Clinical Deterioration
abstract: Interpretable prediction from longitudinal clinical data requires more than accurate risk estimates: a model should preserve meaningful domain structure, reveal how risk evolves over time, and remain auditable when transferred across heterogeneous healthcare settings. We address this challenge with a Knowledge-Guided Temporal Fuzzy Neural Network (KG-TFNN) that integrates clinically anchored yet trainable fuzzy states, explicit temporal fuzzy-risk and observation-process descriptors, parsimonious additive and cross-feature Sugeno inference, and attention-based temporal aggregation within a single auditable prediction pathway. Unlike approaches that rely primarily on latent representations or post-hoc explanations, KG-TFNN exposes membership evolution, feature-level risk contributions, native rule firing, temporal contributions, and parameter drift for direct structural analysis. We evaluated the framework for predicting a ≧ 2-point increase in Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score within 6 h using patient-disjoint MIMIC-IV development and locked testing, followed by fully frozen transport to the multicenter eICU-CRD database comprising 80,239 patients across 205 hospitals. Explicit temporal representation produced the largest controlled ablation effect on discrimination (ΔAUROC = 0.0510), exceeding the contribution of knowledge-guided initialization alone (ΔAUROC = 0.0061), while structural analyses demonstrated reproducible global behavior and identifiable membership and rule evolution. Although KG-TFNN did not exceed tuned LightGBM in discrimination, it enabled forms of temporal and structural auditing unavailable from predictive performance alone and revealed important limitations in cross-database calibration and patient-specific explanation. These findings establish KG-TFNN as a rigorously evaluated framework for studying the trade-off between predictive performance, semantic interpretability, temporal dynamics, and transportability, providing a reusable design principle for trustworthy longitudinal machine learning rather than a task-specific clinical alarm.

title: Security of AI Systems
abstract: AI systems are not only tools for improving security–they are also targets of attack. In this chapter, we explore the vulnerabilities of machine learning systems to adversarial manipulation, ranging from imperceptible feature-space perturbations to realizable attacks on sensors and inputs. We review key attack strategies, including adversarial examples, poisoning, and evasion, and we survey defenses such as robust training, detection mechanisms, and certified defenses. To illustrate the stakes of these challenges, we present a detailed case study on adversarial robustness in face recognition systems. We emphasize that adversarial robustness is not merely a technical hurdle but a prerequisite for building trust in AI systems deployed in safety-critical domains. We close by identifying open challenges and calling for multidisciplinary research to develop AI systems that remain resilient in the face of evolving threats.

title: Design science research in developing a religious chatbot based on Bulugh al-Maram
abstract: Chatbots have recently gained significant popularity. For instance, ChatGPT has become a preferred tool for many individuals seeking instant answers without relying on human responses. This immediacy sets chatbots apart from books, which require users to search for information manually. This time-consuming process does not align with millennials' preference for convenience and efficiency. Studying hadith independently using the Bulugh al-Maram book demands considerable time and effort. The limited use of natural language processing technologies in religious chatbots restricts their ability to handle complex inquiries effectively. A chatbot capable of answering hadith-related questions could greatly assist the public in studying hadith texts by providing direct responses without extensive searching. This chatbot was designed for web browsers, utilizing deep learning as its core technology. This research led to the development of a chatbot prototype for learning hadith from Bulugh al-Maram. Built using the design science research (DSR) methodology, the prototype achieves an intent recognition rate (IRR) of 86.82%. However, its capabilities are below the BERT model, demonstrating a strong ability to accurately interpret user questions and statements.

title: Beyond spatial alignment: Spatial-frequency mutual reconstruction for few-shot fine-grained image classification
abstract: Few-shot fine-grained image classification aims to recognize novel sub-categories from extremely limited labeled data. Recent methods have achieved promising results through dense feature matching or mutual reconstruction to address spatial misalignment. However, most of them operate only in the spatial domain and treat all frequency components and spatial patches equally. As a result, they often overemphasize background layout while weakening the high-frequency textural cues that are critical for fine-grained recognition. To address this limitation, we propose the Spatial-Frequency Mutual Reconstruction Network (SFMR), which explicitly models feature representations in both the spatial and frequency domains. First, a Locality-Aware Feature Enhancement (LAFE) module introduces a learnable 2D geometric distance penalty into self-attention, helping preserve local structural topology that standard Transformers tend to weaken. Second, an Adaptive Frequency Decoupling (AFD) module employs the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) and continuous learnable masks to separate feature maps into low-frequency structural and high-frequency textural streams. Finally, a Saliency-Weighted Mutual Distance (SWMD) metric computes reconstruction errors independently in the two streams and aggregates them with foreground-aware patch weights. A lightweight saliency predictor dynamically estimates patch importance so that the final distance emphasizes informative object regions rather than background noise. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that SFMR captures discriminative details effectively and achieves highly competitive performance.

title: EmbeddGAN: A Novel GAN Framework Using an Embedding Network and Gini Distance Correlation
abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have demonstrated strong performance in generating high-quality synthetic data. However, they are limited by no formal guarantees regarding convergence and the effectiveness of the learning process. In practice, this leads to training instability, mode collapse, and sensitivity to hyperparameters. To address this, we propose EmbeddGAN, a novel adversarial training framework based on a dependence-based objective. Instead of relying on a discriminator that classifies samples as real or fake, EmbeddGAN introduces an embedding network that learns a representation in which statistical dependence between samples and their real/fake labels is maximized, while the generator is trained to minimize this dependence. This objective is implemented using the Gini distance correlation (gCor), which equals zero if and only if the embeddings are statistically independent of the real/fake label. Minimizing this objective therefore encourages real and generated samples to become statistically indistinguishable in the learned embedding space. The embedding network projects both real and generated data into a shared low-dimensional space, where distributional discrepancies can be measured directly through pairwise distances. We adopt a minimax training strategy: the embedding network maximizes the Gini distance correlation (maximizing dependence), while the generator minimizes it (minimizing dependence). Experiments on the MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CelebA datasets demonstrate that EmbeddGAN achieves competitive performance relative to established baselines while exhibiting notably stable training dynamics on the evaluated datasets.

title: PSEE: Progressive Sensor Event Expansion for Point-Supervised Temporal Action Localization
abstract: Temporal action localization (TAL) in wearable sensor streams identifies action classes and temporal boundaries, enabling finer-grained activity understanding than conventional action recognition. However, training typically requires costly start--end annotations for every action instance. To reduce this burden, we study point-supervised TAL, where each instance is labeled with only one timestamp and its class. We propose Progressive Sensor Event Expansion (PSEE), which combines semantic activations, sensor-specific transition evidence, and adaptive temporal ownership to recover point-supervised pseudo segments. These segments supervise standard TAL detectors without modifying their inference procedures. Cross-subject experiments on four inertial-sensing benchmarks demonstrate improved pseudo-boundary quality over adapted point-supervised baselines, compatibility with different TAL detectors, and robustness to point sampling. Code is available at https://github.com/joeeeeyin/PSEE.

title: Hand-Aware Transition Modeling for Bimanual Procedural Anomaly Detection
abstract: Procedural anomaly detection in bimanual assembly requires judging each hand action against the execution so far. A corrective action may look unusual in isolation, while a visually plausible action can violate the order of the procedure. We present HACT, a transition model over predicted per-hand events. A role-preserving history keeps the concurrent responsibilities of both hands, and a marked temporal point process assigns each observed transition a semantic and temporal surprisal. A supervised evidence head and a two-state filter convert these surprisals into per-hand anomaly posteriors. A recovery-aware protocol on predicted events and participant-disjoint folds reports the recovery false-positive rate at an operating point selected on validation participants. On two bimanual power-tool procedures HACT has the highest AUPRC and F1 among the compared methods and the fewest recovery alarms. Applied without retraining to a different assembly order of the same product, it retains the highest AUPRC and F1. The source code is available at https://github.com/Kratos-Wen/HACT.

title: Efficient Online Sampled String Matching
abstract: Efficient Online Sampled String Matching La recherche de chaînes est essentielle dans divers domaines informatiques, notamment la récupération de texte, la bioinformatique et la cybersécurité. Bien que les algorithmes classiques de recherche en ligne et hors ligne offrent des solutions performantes, ils présentent souvent des limitations en termes de temps de recherche ou de mémoire. Les techniques d’indexation hors ligne, permettent des requêtes rapides mais nécessitent un stockage considérable, les rendant impraticables pour des ensembles de données à grande échelle. Pour surmonter ces limites, la recherche de chaînes échantillonnée a émergé comme une alternative efficace en termes d’espace, réduisant l’utilisation de la mémoire tout en préservant l’efficacité de la recherche.Cette thèse explore les avancées en matière de recherche de chaînes échantillonnée, en se concentrant sur le Character Distance Sampling (CDS), une méthode qui enregistre les distances relatives entre les caractères plutôt que leurs positions absolues afin de minimiser les besoins en espace. Bien que le CDS améliore l’efficacité, il rencontre des difficultés avec les alphabets de petite taille et un coût élevé d’indexation. Pour remédier à ces problèmes, ce travail introduit le Character Context Sampling (CCS), une amélioration qui exploite la distribution locale des caractères pour affiner l’échantillonnage et améliorer la précision de la recherche. De plus, une optimisation basée sur la couverture d’ensemble est proposée afin de sélectionner de manière systématique les caractères pivot, réduisant ainsi la taille de l’index sans compromettre les performances.Les résultats expérimentaux montrent que ces techniques surpassent les méthodes existantes, tant en termes d’efficacité spatiale que de performance. En comblant l’écart entre l’indexation traditionnelle et la recherche en ligne, les approches proposées offrent une solution évolutive et efficace pour la recherche de motifs dans des environnements de grande taille et contraints en mémoire. Ce travail contribue au développement de systèmes de recherche textuelle plus performants, en particulier pour les applications en big data et en bioinformatique.

title: Attention Is All You Need: A Technical Review of the Transformer Architecture and Its Impact on Modern Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This technical review examines the Transformer architecture introduced in “Attention Is All You Need,” with emphasis on self-attention, scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding, and the encoder-decoder architecture. It analyzes how the Transformer addressed computational limitations of recurrent sequence models and reviews the experimental evidence presented in the original work. The paper further examines the architectural influence of the Transformer on subsequent developments including GPT, BERT, Transformer-XL, Reformer, Longformer, GPT-3, and Vision Transformer. Limitations involving quadratic attention complexity, long-context processing, computational requirements, and interpretability are also discussed, together with directions for future research.

title: How to Measure a Mind
abstract: If we want to create machines “capable of performing cognitive tasks at our level,” we need a list of abilities we want to examine and a method for doing so. For convenience we will borrow ideas and terms from human psychology. The psychometry of people has been around for over a century; the psychometry of machines is just beginning.

title: THE PROOF IS IN THE CHECKING
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the question: what is a formal logical proof (in general—as opposed to: what is a formal proof in this or that specific proof system)? I begin by setting out a core conception of formal proof and substantiating its designation as ‘core’. The heart of this conception is that there must be an effective or mechanical procedure for checking the correctness of a purported proof. I then consider a proposed strengthening of this conception—one that has become standard in the literature on propositional proof complexity—according to which the proof-checking procedure must be able to be carried out in polynomial time. I discuss a variety of arguments in favour of the strengthened conception—and reject them all. My conclusion is that, when it comes to analysing the very idea of formal logical proof, we have no good reason to move to the strengthened conception and should stick with the core conception.

title: Can Adversarial Attacks Target Cutting‐Edge Language Models Fine‐Tuned for Hate Speech and Toxicity Detection?—A State‐of‐the‐Art Evaluation and Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT The advent of the transformer architecture and its different variants have led to tremendous improvement in several fields lying under the domain of NLP. However, recent studies have conclusively demonstrated that these models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. At the same time, studies related to attacks on language models fine‐tuned for tasks with real‐world security implications are still limited. One such task is automated content moderation, that is, the detection and removal of hateful, offensive, or toxic remarks online. Though the automation of this task provides several advantages, primarily the ability to handle humongous volumes of data, it comes with the disadvantage of being vulnerable to adversarial manipulations. This study serves to perform adversarial experiments on a diverse set of transformer models fine‐tuned on two offensive and toxic content detection datasets. By catering to a diverse set of models differing in architectural design, pre‐training objectives and computational efficacy, this paper seeks to provide a comprehensive evaluation and analysis of adversarial robustness in the context of hate speech and toxicity detection. The presented findings reveal deep‐rooted concerns regarding the reliability and security of these models in real‐world applications, thereby underscoring the critical need to enhance their robustness.

title: Rethinking Vision Architectures with Gated Linear Attention and KAN
abstract: Vision Transformers devote most of their parameters to MLPs for channel mixing, but still rely on quadratic multi-head self-attention for token interactions. While linear attention fixes the complexity problem, bringing it down to O(N), it is usually just paired with the same fixed-activation MLP as before. Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks take a different approach, placing learnable univariate functions on the edges instead. However, existing vision KANs either retain standard attention or remove attention entirely, so the two ideas have not been effectively combined. We introduce LKAT (Linear Kolmogorov-Arnold Transformer) to close this gap: an isotropic ViT-style encoder that couples chunk-wise Gated Linear Attention with a two-layer KAN feed-forward block, backed by an I/O-aware fused RBF-KAN kernel to make radial-basis grid functions efficient in practice. Under a shared DeiT-style training recipe, LKAT-B outperforms ViT-B/16, ViT-5-B, and Mixer-B/16 on ImageNet-100, while Tiny, Small, and Base variants scale consistently on CIFAR-10/100. ImageNet-100 pretraining also transfers effectively to CIFAR fine-tuning, suggesting that gated linear attention and KAN-based radial basis functions provide complementary inductive biases for mid-scale visual representation learning. Code: https://github.com/mehizelali/linear-kan-transformer

title: AtomEgo: Exploring Ego-Robot Integration for Embodied Foundation Model Pretraining
abstract: Embodied foundation models are constrained by the limited scale and diversity of robot demonstrations, motivating the use of large-scale egocentric human interaction data. However, how to effectively incorporate such data into embodied-model pre-training remains unclear because of substantial embodiment and action-space gaps between humans and robots. We present AtomEgo, a systematic study of ego--robot co-training supported by a curated corpus of approximately 2,659 hours and a scalable data processing pipeline. Across vision--language--action and world--action model architectures, we investigate three representative paradigms: joint co-training with domain-specific action heads, progressive ego-to-robot transfer through embodiment alignment, and joint video--action modeling. We evaluate these paradigms through multi-task real-robot experiments and language-conditioned cross-embodiment representation analysis. Our results reveal a simple principle: Data Scale * Alignment Quality --> Capability Gain; egocentric data can improve generalization, but their value depends on how effectively they are aligned and utilized. This principle can provide practical guidance for scalable ego--robot pre-training.

title: OnomatoBridge: Onomatopoeia Translation and Rendering Pipeline in Manga
abstract: Manga is a comic drawn by black and white paints gaining popularity around the world. Onomatopoeia in Manga specifically appeals to the audience with its unique visual styles, which convey sound, motion, and emotion. Visual onomatopoeia translation requires the clean replacement of Japanese onomatopoeia with onomatopoeia in the other language while preserving their visual style. Existing approaches often produce residual artifacts or style inconsistency when removing the Japanese onomatopoeia and rendering stylized English onomatopoeia. To approach these problems, we present OnomatoBridge, a filtering pipeline for visual onomatopoeia translation. We evaluate OnomatoBridge from Japanese to English on the Manga109 onomatopoeia dataset and compare it with baseline image editing models. Experimental results show that the filtered outputs by the proposed method outperform those of conventional methods. OnomatoBridge improves English text correctness by roughly 10 to 25 points and reduces residual Japanese text by about 20 to 50% in relative terms.

title: Disseny i implementació d'una arquitectura multiagent per a consultes en l'àmbit empresarial
abstract: [ES] Las organizaciones gestionan su conocimiento a través de múltiples sistemas: bases de datos operacionales, plataformas de soporte, repositorios documentales y sistemas de gestión de incidencias. Consultar esta información de forma ágil exige que el usuario conozca cada herramienta por separado, lo que representa una barrera de acceso considerable en el trabajo diario. Este trabajo de fin de grado aborda el diseño y desarrollo de la arquitectura del sistema AHORABrain, una plataforma de acceso centralizado al conocimiento empresarial que permite realizar consultas en lenguaje natural sobre fuentes de datos heterogéneas. La aportación principal se centra en la capa de inteligencia que gobierna el sistema: el agente orquestador y la arquitectura multiagente que lo sustenta. El trabajo analiza y justifica por qué una arquitectura de agentes especializados ofrece ventajas frente a un agente único generalista en términos de precisión, control de alucinaciones y escalabilidad. Se diseña el mecanismo por el que el orquestador clasifica la intención de cada consulta y delega en el agente especializado adecuado: un agente orientado a datos estructurados o un agente orientado a contenido textual vectorizado. Cuando la respuesta requiere combinar ambas fuentes, el orquestador coordina la ejecución en paralelo y consolida los resultados en una única respuesta coherente. El trabajo forma parte de un proyecto de equipo en el que otros miembros desarrollan la integración con las fuentes de datos concretas: la base de datos vectorial de tickets de incidencias y el procesamiento de documentos mediante técnicas de chunking y embeddings. La arquitectura diseñada en este trabajo establece el contrato de comunicación entre el orquestador y estos agentes, de forma que nuevas fuentes puedan incorporarse sin necesidad de rediseñar el sistema. El resultado es un producto mínimo viable (MVP) funcional que demuestra la viabilidad del enfoque y sienta las bases para la evolución del sistema hacia nuevas fuentes de datos corporativas en fases posteriores.

title: Navigating State Drift in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Agents: A Diagnostic Benchmark and Structured Graph-Guided Repair Framework
abstract: Multi-turn Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) agents are increasingly relied upon to integrate conversational history, external knowledge retrieval, tool use, and persistent memory. However, their failures extend beyond isolated hallucinations to a more systemic and gradual degradation we term state drift, a phenomenon where the agent progressively loses alignment with the user's current goal, active constraints, retrieved evidence, tool observations, or updated memory. This paper offers three contributions. First, we formalize state drift and introduce a comprehensive taxonomy covering goal, constraint, evidence, retrieval, tool-state, memory, and abstention drift. Second, we present DRIFTBENCH, a diagnostic benchmark featuring controlled state perturbations and fine-grained state-level annotations to systematically elicit and measure drift in RAG agents. Third, we propose SAGE-R, a model-agnostic state-graph framework that diagnoses drift in real time and triggers typed repair actions including rollback, re-retrieval, tool cross-validation, clarification, and abstention. The current repository provides a deterministic v0 scaffold with generated examples, baseline proxies, repair traces, analysis tables, and a human-validation packet, establishing a validated research pipeline prior to the integration of external datasets, model-backed experiments, and completed human annotation. All quantitative results reported in this paper are therefore scaffold-level pipeline validations rather than model-backed empirical findings. Our work lays the foundation for building more reliable, state-aware RAG agents that resist drift across complex multi-turn interactions.

title: Classificação Binária de Lesões Mamárias via Modelos Híbridos: Uma Análise Sob Partição em Nível de Paciente e Diluição Dimensional
abstract: O desenvolvimento de sistemas de Diagnóstico Auxiliado por Computador (CAD) clinicamente viáveis requer rigor contra o vazamento de dados (data leakage) e análise de desafios práticos como o desbalanceamento de classes. Este trabalho avalia um pipeline de classificação binária (Benigno vs. Suspeito) na base INbreast, utilizando o algoritmo Random Forest sob três abordagens de atributos: de Haralick (10), profundos (2048 da ResNet-50) e híbridos. Sob um protocolo estrito de partição em nível de paciente (patient-level split) e validação multissemente, o modelo profundo com acurácia global (64,65% ± 2,68%) com sensibilidade ( 26,14% ± 2,13%) e especificidade (81,35% ± 2,52%) e o híbrido (65,53% ± 3,01%) sensibilidade (27,28% ± 2,47%) e especificidade (83,14% ± 3,18%) operaram em paridade estatística (Wilcoxon, p = 0,3125). A análise de importância Out-of-Bag confirmou a ocorrência de diluição dimensional, relegando o melhor descritor textural à 97ª posição geral. Ademais, o desbalanceamento da base (73,33% de benignos) enviesou a impureza de Gini, resultando em alta especificidade (erro de 11,85% para BI-RADS 2), mas comprometendo as classes de transição (BI-RADS 3 e 4a). O estudo estabelece uma linha de base diagnóstica honesta, apontando o balanceamento via SMOTE e a seleção ativa de atributos como caminhos futuros.

evidence.title: Classificação Binária de Lesões Mamárias via Modelos Híbridos: Uma Análise Sob Partição em Nível de Paciente e Diluição Dimensional
evidence.abstract: O desenvolvimento de sistemas de Diagnóstico Auxiliado por Computador (CAD) clinicamente viáveis requer rigor contra o vazamento de dados (data leakage) e análise de desafios práticos como o desbalanceamento de classes. Este trabalho avalia um pipeline de classificação binária (Benigno vs. Suspeito) na base INbreast, utilizando o algoritmo Random Forest sob três abordagens de atributos: de Haralick (10), profundos (2048 da ResNet-50) e híbridos. Sob um protocolo estrito de partição em nível de paciente (patient-level split) e validação multissemente, o modelo profundo com acurácia global (64,65% ± 2,68%) com sensibilidade ( 26,14% ± 2,13%) e especificidade (81,35% ± 2,52%) e o híbrido (65,53% ± 3,01%) sensibilidade (27,28% ± 2,47%) e especificidade (83,14% ± 3,18%) operaram em paridade estatística (Wilcoxon, p = 0,3125). A análise de importância Out-of-Bag confirmou a ocorrência de diluição dimensional, relegando o melhor descritor textural à 97ª posição geral. Ademais, o desbalanceamento da base (73,33% de benignos) enviesou a impureza de Gini, resultando em alta especificidade (erro de 11,85% para BI-RADS 2), mas comprometendo as classes de transição (BI-RADS 3 e 4a). O estudo estabelece uma linha de base diagnóstica honesta, apontando o balanceamento via SMOTE e a seleção ativa de atributos como caminhos futuros.

title: Replication package for "Which Model Wrote This? Version-Level Attribution Across Six Languages, and What Survives a Language Boundary"
abstract: Analysis code, generation harness, prompts in six languages, derived statistics and a human-corpus manifest for a study of within-language attribution of nine 2025 and 2026 language models and human text in English, Polish, Finnish, Swedish, German and Russian (6,000 documents, 100 topics per language). title: A Control Framework for Digital Asset Provenance and Intellectual Property in Creative AI Abstract.
abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into creative production pipelines introduces acute vulnerabilities regarding intellectual property (IP) infringement, unauthorized data scraping, and the erosion of digital provenance. Existing information security standards (such as NIST CSF and CIS Controls) primarily address enterprise IT infrastructure rather than the distinct lifecycle of digital media and algorithmic assets. This paper introduces the Creative Digital & AI Content Security Framework (CDAC-SF), an operational standard designed to govern IP strategy, enforce cryptographic provenance, and mitigate algorithmic risk across the creative lifecycle.

title: The Corporate Impact of Artificial Intelligence by 2035
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transitioning from a technology primarily used for prediction, recommendation, and content generation toward systems capable of reasoning, using external tools, executing multi-step workflows, and interacting with the physical environment. Recent developments in foundation models, multimodal AI, reasoning models, AI agents, robotics, specialized AI infrastructure, and on-device inference indicate that the role of AI within corporations is likely to expand substantially during the next decade. This thesis investigates the potential impact of AI/ML technology on corporate sectors by 2035 using current technological developments and evidence published by organizations including OpenAI, Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, Anthropic, the International Labour Organization (ILO), OECD, and NIST. Current enterprise evidence already indicates a transition from experimental AI usage toward workflow integration. OpenAI reports substantial increases in enterprise usage and reasoning workloads, while Anthropic and other technology companies are developing systems capable of autonomous multi-step task execution. The research examines five major technological trajectories: advanced reasoning, agentic AI, multimodal and embodied AI, AI infrastructure, and AI governance/security. Their potential effects are analyzed across information technology, finance, healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, retail, telecommunications, professional services, and human resources. The thesis argues that the most significant corporate transformation by 2035 is unlikely to be simply the replacement of human employees with AI. Instead, the more plausible transformation is the restructuring of work itself: AI systems will increasingly perform routine cognitive tasks, coordinate workflows, generate and analyze information, operate software systems, and potentially control physical machines. Consequently, organizations are likely to shift toward human-AI collaboration, smaller highly skilled teams, AI-supervised operations, continuous reskilling, and stronger governance mechanisms.

title: Quantum Radar Through Entanglement‑Based Illumination: A Framework for Enhanced Target Detection
abstract: Quantum radar systems leverage entangled photon pairs to detect and identify targets in noisy or cluttered environments with sensitivity beyond classical limits. By transmitting one photon of an entangled pair toward a distant object while retaining its partner locally, the system exploits quantum correlations to improve signal discrimination, reduce noise susceptibility, and enhance detection probability. This paper outlines the physical principles, operational architecture, and performance advantages of entanglement‑based illumination, providing a clear foundation for future quantum‑enhanced sensing technologies.(If you want it shorter, longer, or more formal, tap: shorter paragraph, longer paragraph, more formal)

title: On the Minimization of Graph Counterfactual Explanations: Theory and a Local Bounded Search Algorithm
abstract: Abstract Graph counterfactual explainability (GCE) addresses the interpretability limitations of opaque machine learning models on graph-structured data by producing graph counterfactuals (GCs): alternative graphs that remain maximally similar to a given instance while inducing a different model prediction. State-of-the-art GCE methods usually follow a generate-and-minimize pipeline: first, generate a valid counterfactual, then refine it to be closer to the original graph. While generation is well-studied, minimization still lacks a formal definition, complexity analysis, and general-purpose algorithms; existing solutions are either simple random edge-swap heuristics or tightly coupled to specific generators, limiting effectiveness and generality. In this work, we address a key gap in GCE by providing the first principled study of minimizing a given valid graph counterfactual. We formalize the task as an optimization problem and prove it is NP-hard. We then propose a decoupled generate-and-minimize framework and introduce Local Bounded Search (LBS), a model-agnostic heuristic that refines any valid counterfactual via constrained structural and attribute edits to reduce dissimilarity while preserving validity. Across nine synthetic and real-world datasets (molecular, biomedical, social), LBS reduces structural edit distance by up to 98% from the initial counterfactual and consistently outperforms existing refinement heuristics.

title: Event-Frame Fusion for Inter-Frame Segmentation via Event-Guided Motion
abstract: Autonomous navigation requires precise and efficient semantic segmentation, yet existing frame-based approaches remain limited by motion blur, glare, latency, and the low temporal resolution (20-30 FPS) of conventional cameras, which leads to information loss between frames. Event cameras have emerged as an alternative sensing modality, capturing intensity changes asynchronously with high temporal resolution, high dynamic range, and sparse outputs. However, event-based algorithms still fall short of frame-based ones in accuracy, as most segmentation methods are designed for dense frame data. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid vision architecture that combines conventional frame-based and event-based cameras. The system integrates two complementary components: (1) a compact Spiking Neural Network (SNN) with 42k parameters for motion estimation, and (2) a lightweight event-driven SNN with 0.84M parameters for frame-based semantic segmentation, which interpolates motion between frames to refine segmentation results. By predicting inter-frame segmentations, the framework achieves segmentation rates of up to 500 Hz with an energy consumption below 1.87 mJ per inference, while maintaining real-time GPU execution at frequencies up to 200 Hz. Additionally, our approach compensates for information loss in frames affected by blur or overexposure, enabling more robust perception in challenging conditions.

title: Per-Aetiology Contrastive Severity Embeddings with Phonological Pseudo-Labelling for Multilingual Dysarthric Speech
abstract: Most multilingual dysarthria-severity systems either train on a single aetiology-language pair or pool heterogeneous aetiologies into one label space. We test that pooling assumption with four matched HuBERT-base contrastive embedding models under a shared backbone, training recipe, corpus registry and held-out evaluation: one mixed-aetiology baseline and three aetiology-specific models for cerebral palsy (CP), Parkinson's disease (PD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Training combines clinically labelled speech with ordinal pseudo-labels from a training-free phonological profiling method [1], [2]. On speaker-disjoint, leakage-filtered held-out subsets, the per-aetiology models outperform the mixed baseline across all three target aetiologies: CP (macro F1 0.829 vs 0.676, +22.6 % relative), PD (0.715 vs 0.511, +40.0 %) and ALS (0.788 vs 0.596, +32.3 %). On CP, adding 144 SAP and 44 CDSD pseudo-labelled speakers lifts macro F1 from 0.786 to 0.829 over a clinical-only CP model (+4.3 percentage points). Training data span three to seven languages per aetiology. We position this as a controlled comparison of label-space design choices and discuss pseudo-label calibration, split hygiene, and confidence-thresholded deployment as important limitations for future work.

title: Logics of Filter Bubbles
abstract: Filter bubbles can be understood as configurations characterized by within-group proximity and separation from outsiders. Personalized feeds may form or preserve such configurations. We develop hybrid-style logics for reasoning about filter bubbles. The static logic characterizes bubble-shaped configurations, while its dynamic extension captures their formation and persistence under personalized feeds. We provide sound and strongly complete axiomatizations for the static and dynamic logics and prove their decidability.

title: Reliability-Centered Evaluation of Sparse Longitudinal CT Lesion-Size Forecasting with Conformal Interval Calibration and Gompertz-Inspired Regularization
abstract: Sparse longitudinal CT follow-up limits lesion-size forecasting when only a few prior observations are available. We constructed a five-visit DLT-derived same-lesion trajectory benchmark from DeepLesion and Deep Lesion Tracker (DLT), yielding 205 trajectories from 129 patients. We compared an exploratory conventional sparse-to-final analysis with a primary fixed visit-index horizon design predicting the common log change from T3 to T4 while progressively adding earlier observations, evaluating predictive accuracy, uncertainty reliability, post-hoc conformal interval calibration, subgroup performance, and Gompertz-inspired trajectory regularization. The evaluated methods showed partially overlapping point-prediction accuracy but distinct uncertainty behavior. Mean held-out RMSE across ten training seeds was 0.4726, 0.4305, 0.4499, and 0.4513 for m = 1, 2, 3, 4, indicating the lowest mean RMSE at m = 2; additional history did not improve RMSE. At m = 4, raw Cohort-Level Feature GP coverage was near the 95% nominal level, whereas MC Dropout, Deep Ensemble, and residual-scale intervals were conservative. Patient-level conformal calibration generally produced near-nominal or conservative coverage at the cost of wider intervals. Patient-grouped development cross-validation selected lambda* = 0 for the Gompertz-inspired term. A global population reference frequently opposed lesion-level change directions, and prediction difficulty varied across anatomical subgroups. Overall, additional historical observations provided limited predictive benefit once the prediction horizon was controlled, while predictive accuracy, uncertainty reliability, and trajectory consistency did not necessarily improve together, and should be evaluated jointly in sparse longitudinal imaging.

title: Desenrotllament de les nostres primeres xarxes de neurones artificials per a la seua aplicació en un videojoc First Person Shooter
abstract: [ES] La industria de los videojuegos emplea habitualmente Máquinas de Estados Finitos (FSM) y Árboles de Comportamiento para controlar a los personajes no jugadores (NPCs). Aunque eficientes, estas técnicas generan comportamientos rígidamente deterministas, predecibles y susceptibles a ser explotados por los usuarios. Este Trabajo Final de Grado propone el diseño, implementación y evaluación de un agente inteligente autónomo capaz de aprender a jugar en un entorno tridimensional de disparos en primera persona (FPS) sin depender de lógicas preprogramadas. Para lograr este objetivo, se ha desarrollado una arquitectura computacional basada en el paradigma de la neuroevolución, combinando Redes Neuronales Artificiales superficiales y Algoritmos Genéticos. El sistema ha sido programado íntegramente de forma nativa en C# sobre el motor gráfico Unity, garantizando un rendimiento óptimo en tiempo real. El agente percibe su entorno dinámico mediante un sistema de sensores espaciales proyectivos (Raycasts) y optimiza su toma de decisiones tácticas (locomoción, recolección de recursos vitales y combate) a través de un proceso iterativo guiado por una función de aptitud (fitness) multivariable. El entrenamiento del agente se estructuró aplicando la técnica de Curriculum Learning, incrementando la complejidad de los estímulos de manera escalonada. Los resultados experimentales demuestran que el sistema es capaz de superar vulnerabilidades heurísticas severas, tales como la explotación de recompensas (Reward Hacking), los máximos locales y el olvido catastrófico. En conclusión, el proyecto valida la viabilidad técnica y la eficiencia computacional de los métodos neuroevolutivos para la generación de comportamientos tácticos adaptativos y emergentes dentro del sector del entretenimiento interactivo.

title: CNN-LSTM Autoencoder for Behavioral Anomaly Detection in Children with ASD
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by differences in social communication and repetitive behavioral patterns. Behavioral analysis based on video is commonly performed through manual observation, which can be time-consuming and subjective. This study proposes a CNN-LSTM Autoencoder approach to detect behavioral anomalies in children with ASD based on video data. The CNN Autoencoder extracts spatial features from video frames, while the LSTM Autoencoder learns temporal patterns from sequential features. The model was trained using 88 videos collected from children with ASD, while five videos from a public dataset were used for testing. The experimental results produced mean reconstruction errors of 0.1000, 0.1184, and 0.2079 for the training, validation, and testing data, respectively, with a threshold of 0.2520. Among 65 testing sequences, 51 were classified as in-distribution with respect to the ASD training data, while 14 were identified as anomalies. These results indicate that the proposed approach can identify behavioral deviations from the learned ASD behavioral distribution. However, the system is not intended to provide a clinical diagnosis of ASD.

title: Linceu: A Metrologically Calibrated Computational Pathology Framework for Topology-Aware Tissue Segmentation in Leprosy Whole Slide Images
abstract: The Bacillary Index used in Ridley-Hilson leprosy classification remains tied to physical high-power fields defined by optical microscope objectives and eyepiece Field Number, while Whole Slide Imaging systems rely on pixel-based coordinate systems. This mismatch creates a calibration gap for pathologists and researchers working in Computational Pathology on leprosy slides. This study introduces a Python framework that maps physical areas onto calibrated digital Regions of Interest directly from BigTIFF WSI images, extracting on-the-fly ROI tensors, without static tiling. To ensure spatial reliability, the framework’s pixel-to-physical unit conversion was rigorously validated against a certified stage micrometer, achieving a high-precision resolution of 0.2703 MPP with a minimal relative error of 0.074%. Based on this verified calibration, Topological Data Analysis (TDA) was employed to automate tissue/background classification on Fite-Faraco stained slides using persistent homology to characterize dense Mycobacterium leprae globi and surrounding morphology. Five anonymized WSIs from CREDESH/HC-UFU/HU BRASIL were processed, yielding a total of 6,804 ROIs classified as tissue or background, and then validated against manually annotated ground truth on 1,500 stratified ROIs across the five slides. This resulted in a Dice coefficient of 97.42% and IoU of 94.97%, indicating that persistent homology and TDA-driven results can assist with computational pathology segmentation on leprosy slides. Future work must extend the tissue/background triage beyond classification, toward automated Bacillary Index estimation using neural network architectures for bacilli detection, as a step toward the development of a computer-aideddiagnosis (CAD) system for leprosy.

title: Artificial intelligence, standards and patents
abstract: This chapter examines the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI), technical standards and patents. It first considers how standards may operationalise requirements for trustworthy AI, especially under the EU AI Act. It considers the limits of industry-led standardisation, the need for democratic scrutiny, and the role of harmonised standards in translating statutory duties into practice for AI providers. It also compares horizontal standards applicable across AI systems with sector-specific standards designed to address particular technologies, uses, and risks. The chapter then shifts from AI as an object of standardisation to AI as a tool operating within the broader standardisation ecosystem, especially in AI-assisted patent essentiality determinations. AI can certainly facilitate patent searching, document analysis and portfolio management, but it cannot currently replace expert assessment, as existing literature has stressed. title: Design of an Intelligent Five-Stage Zero-Knowledge Proof Synthesis and Deployment Framework for Lightweight Cryptographic Assurance in Wearable IoT Systems
abstract: Wearable IoT systems need cryptographic assurances to protect user privacy without depleting device resources in continuous sensing contexts with limited battery and memory. Though mathematically elegant, zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) architectures assume continuous compute budgets, enormous constraint systems, and large gadget integrations that raise latency and energy costs make them unsuitable for wearable. These constraints distinguish theoretical ZKP efficiency from IoT hardware limitations. An entire hardware-aware ZKP synthesis and deployment pipeline for wearable devices is shown here. The framework uses five novel analytical methods. Micro-cycle-level execution traces are used to produce Adaptive Proof Footprint Maps that fit the device&s;s dynamic compute envelope by MC-AZKP. These maps en-able Progressive Constraint Folding (PCF-ZKP) of large constraint sets into folded polynomials with strong sparsity retention. ZeLP-Fusion embeds ZKP logic in lightweight primitives like Ascon, PRESENT, and ECC for proof-carrying encryption without devices and deployments. HyFSS creates compact proofs with reduced verification pressure utilizing weighted non- inter-active challenges for fused constraint geometry deployment. Final proofs are examined by W- PEVF in real wearable contexts for security drift, battery impact, and runtime stability. In next- generation wearable IoT contexts, these advances minimize proof size, compute cycles, and battery consumption while maintaining security guarantees, enabling privacy-preserving authentication and secure data transmissions.

title: A reproducible entropy-weighted Gower-CLARA-TOPSIS procedure for mixed-type MSME segmentation and prioritization
abstract: In this paper a reproducible approach for segmentation of mixed-type data and the within-cluster prioritizing is presented. The procedure keeps raw categorical values for Gower dissimilarity, binary or count representations only for entropy weighting, applies CLARA to repeated samples with PAM medoids, and evaluates weighted and Top-N feature configurations with the Silhouette Coefficient, medoid-based Davies-Bouldin Index, and Calinski-Harabasz Index. The chosen configuration is then utilized to rank within clusters, instead of between clusters using TOPSIS to evaluate the economic-operational preparedness of similar firms. It presents a worked example with 1049 de-duplicated MSME records from Sampang, Indonesia, with numerical, binary, count and categorical attributes. The optimum configuration selected four operational and financial aspects and increased the Silhouette Coefficient from 0.4183 to 0.5588, decreased the Davies-Bouldin Index from 1.2393 to 0.6181, and boosted the Calinski-Harabasz Index from 357.7787 to 992.3958. By combining entropy-based feature weighting, weighted Gower dissimilarity, CLARA sampling, and Top-N feature selection, the procedure provides transparent mixed-data segmentation while preserving categorical semantics and separating clustering from peer-group-based TOPSIS ranking. A reference Jupyter Notebook implementation and an anonymized or de-identified demonstration dataset are supplied to support inspection and reuse of the workflow.

title: Hybrid deep learning framework for AI-generated text detection
abstract: Recently, large language models have demonstrated remarkable ability to generate human-like textual content. This advancement has increased the need for reliable methods to detect AI-generated texts, particularly to address concerns related to academic dishonesty and the spread of misinformation on social media. This study introduces a hybrid deep learning model, which integrates Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks (BiDLSTM), Transformer blocks, and one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks (1D CNNs) to distinguish between AI-generated and human-written texts. The model was evaluated on two diverse datasets, DAIGT and HC3, containing thousands of samples generated by various large language models alongside human-written texts. The proposed model achieved promising performance, with test accuracies of 99.47% on the DAIGT dataset and 97.09% on the HC3 dataset. These results suggest that the hybrid architecture can effectively capture subtle linguistic and stylistic differences between AI-generated and human-written content. This study contributes to ongoing efforts in AI-generated text detection and supports applications aimed at maintaining content authenticity and academic integrity.

title: The Wisdom of Artificial Deliberative Crowds
abstract: The aggregation of many lay estimates often outperforms individual expert judgment, a phenomenon known as the wisdom of crowds. While this is usually attributed to the independence of estimates, an even stronger effect arises through deliberation: averaging the consensus estimates of small deliberating groups outperforms the classical wisdom of crowds, with individual judgments themselves also becoming more accurate after deliberation. Whether these improvements transfer to large language models deliberating amongst themselves is unknown. Here we adapt a three-stage deliberation paradigm previously used with human participants for use with large language models from three different families, and test it across four domains of increasing real-world stakes: visual numerical estimation (Study 1), peer review of machine-learning papers (Study 2), detection of hidden malicious behavior by an artificial intelligence agent (Study 3), and sports forecasting against a real prediction market (Study 4). Across domains, deliberation reduced collective error beyond passive aggregation of independent responses, and post-deliberation individual judgments retained this collective gain. Notably, the advantage required model diversity: groups composed of clones of a single model did not benefit from deliberating. These results establish machine deliberation as a general-purpose aggregation mechanism, and point to diversity as an active ingredient.

title: CompAdapt: Adaptable Composite Motion Modeling for Physics-Consistent Text-to-Video Generation
abstract: While diffusion-based text-to-video (T2V) models have demonstrated impressive capability in generating realistic and temporally coherent videos, they often fail to respect fundamental physical dynamics. Although recent physics-constrained methods incorporate explicit dynamics priors to improve physical plausibility, they remain limited to simple single-type motions, depend on manually specified parameters, and struggle to generalize to unseen physical laws. In this work, we propose CompAdapt, a physics-consistent T2V framework for adaptable generation across complex real-world scenarios. It extends neural dynamics modeling beyond single-type motions to encompass composite physical behaviors, including coupled motions, multi-stage transitions, and multi-object collisions. Furthermore, CompAdapt translates natural language prompts into structured physical semantics, enabling end-to-end specification of motion types, temporal relations, and initial physical parameters. To generalize to novel physical environments, CompAdapt introduces dynamics-aware prior matching, achieving one-shot adaptation without retraining the core dynamics module. In addition, a physics-aware latent feature fusion module improves visual fidelity under fast and complex motion. Experiments on physics-focused T2V benchmarks demonstrate that CompAdapt improves physical consistency over both general T2V models and physics-constrained baselines, while preserving high visual quality and adaptability to unseen dynamics. The project page is available at https://makapic.github.io/CompAdapt/ .

title: AI-GRACE: A Use-Case Operationalization Framework for Agentic AI: From Organizational Objectives and Obligations to Deployment Capabilities and Architecture
abstract: Organizations deploying agentic artificial intelligence must determine more than whether a model is trustworthy; they must establish what to validate, control, and observe for a use case to deliver its intended outcome while meeting applicable obligations. This paper proposes AI-GRACE (Agentic Intelligence-Governance, Risk, Assurance, Controls, and Evidence) as a use-case operationalization framework connecting organizational governance with technical implementation. The proposal draws on professional observations and a purposive synthesis of standards and literature, using design science to frame the method contribution and situational method engineering to guide contextual tailoring and reuse. The framework establishes objectives and obligations and then assesses risks in seven proposed domains, including mission and value realization. It derives requirements for assurance before deployment, runtime controls, and evidence, which guide capability qualification, gap assessment, and a logical architecture. An Agent Operating Envelope specifies permitted actions and escalation conditions, while Risk-Aligned Independence Levels (RAIL) summarize the authorized independence. A fictional retail banking application illustrates the method. The contribution is a traceable basis for deciding what an organization must implement, what it already supports, and what remains unresolved. Empirical evaluation must establish whether it improves deployment decisions, efficiency, and reuse.

title: Plataforma d'aprenentatge d'escacs basada en sistemes multiagent
abstract: [ES] RoninChess es una plataforma web de entrenamiento de ajedrez personalizado que combina la precisión de cálculo del motor Stockfish con la capacidad explicativa de los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM), guiada por un catálogo de conceptos ajedrecísticos redactado por un Maestro FIDE. El sistema resuelve un problema real del jugador de club (1000–2200 ELO): entrenar de forma desorganizada, con motores que dan números sin explicar por qué y sin un plan coherente, frente a un entrenador humano que cuesta entre 25 y 100 e la hora. La solución es un sistema multiagente (implementado con LangGraph) de cinco agentes especializados —Modelo del Alumno, Planificador, Entrenador, Analista y Comunicador— que importan las partidas del usuario desde Lichess y Chess.com, diagnostican sus debilidades a nivel de concepto, generan un plan de entrenamiento adaptativo con repetición espaciada (FSRS) y explican cada error en lenguaje natural adaptado a su nivel. El principio rector es estricto: «Stockfish calcula, el LLM explica, el catálogo guía y el Comunicador presenta»; el LLM nunca evalúa la posición, lo que elimina las alucinaciones ajedrecísticas. El proyecto, desarrollado en solitario siguiendo metodologías Lean Startup, ágil, Spec-Driven y Test-Driven Development, está desplegado en producción (Next.js en Vercel y FastAPI dockerizado en un servidor privado virtual) y se presenta a la vez como trabajo de ingeniería del software y como proyecto de emprendimiento, con su estudio de mercado, modelo de negocio y validación con usuarios.

title: TRUTH SURFACE Research Methodology v1.0
abstract: Formal methodology document for the TRUTH SURFACE series of independent adversarial architectural analyses of AI security vendors and analyst firms. 21 papers published under this methodology. Covers evidence accepted and excluded, independence conditions, limitations including the live fire double standard, full conflict of interest disclosure, the validator problem, relationship to other Red Specter capabilities, and publication standards. Currently under independent audit by Martin McHugh using the Adversarial Verification Protocol. Audit results will be published simultaneously on Zenodo without Red Specter preview or approval.

title: Editorial: Reimagining roles and identity in the era of human - AI collaboration, volume II
abstract: This editorial introduces the second volume of the Research Topic Reimagining Roles and Identities in the Era of Human-Machine Collaboration. Artificial intelligence (AI) no longer merely assists human activity in digital environments , it actively intervenes in and reconfigures it. As AI moves from instrumental tool to affective, social interaction partner, it forces a reckoning with the boundaries of identity and social role that earlier frameworks took for granted (Brandtzaeg et al., 2022). The studies gathered here make a shared argument: human-AI collaboration is not a neutral technological upgrade but an active experiment in reconstructing self-perception, social relations, and behavior. Understanding it requires more than a single disciplinary lens , the behavioral logic and ethical stakes are too entangled to separate. We draw out five main findings that, together, define the contours of this experiment.First, the design of virtual-persona interaction is not incidental, it is a primary lever shaping users' emotional bonds with AI. Realism does not scale linearly with trust: high realism builds attraction and trust, but medium realism can backfire into an "uncanny valley" response (Tao et al.). In e-commerce livestreaming, intelligent virtual hosts can build initial trust and value cocreation, but only within the limits set by users' technology anxiety (Zhong et al.). More strikingly, users are not passive recipients of these designs , they actively construct virtual parents with emotional-support functions through generative AI chatbots, channeling real kinship trauma into a dynamic process of resilience communication (Li et al.). These findings leave little doubt that human-computer interaction design is now doing real psychological and relational work, not merely functional work.Second, AI's acceptance in consumption contexts is far more conditional than technology optimists assume. Labeling content as AI-generated is not a neutral disclosure, which can suppress self-expression by amplifying perceived eeriness and risk, moderated by product type (Cheng & Nam). Trust in AI livestream hosts is not general but transactional: it materializes through functional pathways only when utilitarian motivation is strong, while human hosts retain the upper hand through relational trust (Lin et al.). Perhaps most tellingly, creators themselves do not trust audiences to accept AI involvement, they engage in "AI disguise," concealing AI's role through invisible labor to protect their own credibility, a workaround that quietly produces new inequality among creators (Su et al.). Acceptance of AI, in other words, is being manufactured as much as it is earned.Third, AI's behavioral effects cut both ways, and the studies here refuse to soften that tension. Anthropomorphic AI design boosts value co-creation intentions through social presence, but that gain erodes as users' sense of control increases (Ye et al.). Generative AI simultaneously helps and hollows out student entrepreneurship, strengthening performance through self-efficacy while undermining it through fears of substitution (Yu et al.). And in continued-use decisions, seduction is winning out over fear: pull effects currently outweigh push effects, with digital literacy dampening fear but amplifying seduction (Xia et al.). This is not a story of steady, comfortable adoption, it is one of persistent ambivalence.Fourth, perceived AI attributes are actively reshaping how content circulates and who gets credit for it. An AI source label is enough to discount perceived creative effort, and with it, users' motivation to intervene in algorithmic curation (Lim et al.). Yet AI co-creation is not uniformly devalued which can raise perceived novelty and usefulness above what human collaboration achieves, making it a stronger driver of co-creation intent (Liu et al.). Even in high-stakes settings like policy dissemination, where digital human hosts still lag behind real hosts in effectiveness, that gap narrows substantially once anthropomorphism and credibility endorsement are engineered in (Chen et al.). Perception, not capability alone, is doing much of the work here.Fifth, AI is not simply a source of convenience , it is a generator of anxiety that operates at both the individual and organizational level, and this volume does not shy away from naming it. Emotional cues like emoticons only move brand evaluation under specific cognitive conditions, not universally (Yoon). Emotional trust in AI, once treated as a monolith, in fact fractures into four distinct dimensions: perceived authenticity, emotional validation, emotional recognition, and symbolic connection (Briones-Llamoctanta et al.). And beneath the optimistic surface narrative of workplace AI adoption lies a harder truth: "algorithmic anxiety," rooted in trust rupture and identity crisis, is actively corroding the psychological contract between employees and employers (Shekhar & Saurombe).Taken together, these studies make clear that the behavioral landscape of human-AI collaboration is neither settled nor simple , it is contested terrain, marked by real dialectical tension between benefit and harm, trust and suspicion, empowerment and anxiety. This is precisely the terrain the volume's central proposition demands we confront: technology does not just extend human capability, it forces an ongoing interrogation of what human capability, and human identity, actually mean (Baskerville et al., 2020). The evidence assembled here should be read as a call to action, not just a record of findings. Future research must go further, interrogating the power dynamics (Kellogg et al., 2020), cultural variation, and long-term effects (Glikson & Woolley, 2020) that remain underexamined and design must follow suit, building the inclusive, reflective technological ecosystem (Mittelstadt, 2019) needed to ensure that human agency and the meaning of human connection survive the digital-intelligent wave, rather than being quietly displaced by it.

title: Uncovering the limits of machine learning for software security
abstract: Maschinelles Lernen (ML) ist in der Softwaresicherheitsforschung äußerst populär, doch seine Grenzen wurden kaum untersucht. Diese Arbeit deckt sie auf, zeigt ihre Auswirkungen und eröffnet Wege, sie zu überwinden. Zunächst zeigen wir, dass ML-Techniken zur Schwachstellenerkennung den klassifizierten Code nicht verstehen: Semantikerhaltende Änderungen wie das Umbenennen von Variablen verschlechtern ihre Leistung erheblich, und verwundbare Funktionen lassen sich nicht von ihren gepatchten Versionen unterscheiden. Der Grund: Von 300 manuell geprüften Benchmark-Funktionen lässt sich keine ohne umgebenden Kontext klassifizieren; das vorherrschende Evaluierungsparadigma ist somit grundlegend fehlerhaft. In 72 Publikationen führender Konferenzen identifizieren wir neun methodische Fallstricke, die die Validität der ML-Sicherheitsforschung gefährden. Schließlich zeigen wir, wie Agenten die Grenzen ML-basierter Sicherheitstechniken zu den Grenzen der Berechnung selbst verschieben.

title: LLM Semiotic Capacity
abstract: We introduce a model of Picca’s semiotic channel principle. Semiotics studies how signs produce and communicate meaning. Channel capacity, from information theory, is the theoretical maximum rate at which data can be reliably transmitted over a communication channel, here a LLM used by AI agents.Our semiotic channel communicating meaning is an implicit state machine LLM, where we operationalize meaning using a similarity function. In particular messages are interpreted by those that entail it, and we profile channel capacity by mapping message entropy against interpretation mutual information. LLM that result in profiles with higher overall mutual information are sought for identification, certification and comparison of LLMs. This provides a rigorous and actionable framework for understanding, evaluating, and designing LLM-mediated communication between AI agents.

title: The Intentionality Gap: Reconceptualizing Interpersonal Deception Theory and the Persuasion Knowledge Model for anthropomorphic AI agents
abstract: Interpersonal Deception Theory (IDT) and the Persuasion Knowledge Model (PKM) have anchored the study of deception in marketing communications for three decades. Both assume that communicators possess actual intent: IDT defines deception as a message knowingly transmitted to foster a false belief, and the PKM models consumers’ inference of a communicator’s persuasive intent. Anthropomorphic artificial intelligence (AI) agents, including chatbots, embodied conversational agents, and virtual influencers, violate this assumption: they reliably trigger the trust, suspicion, and credibility judgments that both theories treat as evidence about a sender’s mental states, while lacking psychological intent of their own, even when communicative goals may reside in the organizations, systems, or design choices behind them. This paper introduces the intentionality gap, the mismatch between where consumers attribute intent and where communicative goals actually originate, and develops perceived agent intentionality (PAI) as the construct through which the gap operates. Synthesizing literatures on deception, persuasion knowledge, anthropomorphism, mind perception, dark patterns, and manipulation, the paper reconceptualizes IDT and the PKM around the receiver’s attribution of intent rather than the sender’s possession of it, presents a receiver-centered process model with eight propositions, and outlines a research agenda spanning measurement development, experimentation, and managerial application.

title: Privacy-preserving multimodal student well-being analytics via federated temporal transformers
abstract: Abstract Student well-being analytics may support timely educational assistance, but behavioural, psychological, and academic records are sensitive and difficult to pool. We present a federated temporal Transformer that combines smartphone sensing, ecological momentary assessment (EMA), academic records, and digital behavioural traces while retaining raw records on student clients. Because psychometric variables can overlap with a composite well-being target, evaluation is organized around a leakage-free multimodal protocol, a temporally separated forecasting protocol, and a full-feature diagnostic upper bound. On 48 StudentLife participants, student-level leave-one-student-out predictions yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.834 for centralized training and 0.824 for FedProx ( $$p=0.21$$ ). Record-level differentially private training at $$\varepsilon =4$$ achieved an AUROC of 0.791; the corresponding membership-inference AUROC decreased from 0.92 without privacy noise to 0.64. Including target-overlapping survey variables inflated AUROC by 0.094–0.107, demonstrating why the leakage-free protocol is used for the main claims. Directional findings were reproduced on 497 independent GLOBEM participants, where FedProx achieved an AUROC of 0.783. Cross-modal ablation, calibration, privacy attacks, external validation, and explanation-stability analyses jointly characterize predictive utility and deployment limits. The framework is intended for research and educational risk stratification, not clinical diagnosis or autonomous intervention.

title: The Sources of Unknowability and Self-refutation in Epistemic and Dynamic Epistemic Logic
abstract: In this paper, we define a formula $φ$ to be unbelievable if $\Boxφ$ is unsatisfiable, and unknowable if $\Boxφ\landφ$ is unsatisfiable. We then analyze the sources of unknowability and unbelievability in different classes of frames K, KD, KD45, and S5. We first show that any unbelievable formula is a fixed point of the Moore function defined by $f(φ)=φ\land\lnot\Boxφ.$ Our main result shows that in S5, the static notions of unknowability and unbelievability in epistemic logic, and the dynamic notions of always informativeness and eventual self-refutation in dynamic epistemic logic are all equivalent to ``Moorean phenomena.'' We also generalize the result to the multi-agent case, showing that although all unknowable formulas still manifest Moorean phenomena, new mechanisms arise due to their interactive nature. Finally, we briefly analyze whether the Brandenburger-Keisler paradox in epistemic game theory can be considered Moorean.

title: SWE-Proof: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World Issues with Machine-Checked Proofs?
abstract: Ensuring the correctness of LLM-generated code is a core challenge for modern software engineering. Benchmarks for agentic code generation check correctness with held-out test suites, which are inherently incomplete and increasingly susceptible to memorization. Formal verification avoids both problems, but existing work covers only standalone tasks whose specifications are given as input, not real issues, which touch large repositories and state intent in vague natural language. We present Benchproofer, a pipeline that turns a coding task with a known correct patch into a formally verified one: it writes a specification for the new code, summarizes the existing functions that code calls with axioms, and admits an instance only after mechanical and adversarial gates agree. Applying it to SWE-bench Verified yields SWE-Proof, 500 real issues whose correctness is formally verified rather than tested, and it extends to SWE-bench Pro. Evaluating Claude Opus 4.8, we find that verification catches what tests miss: a quarter of test-passing patches admit counterexamples, which a structured natural-language specification does not fix, while a correct formal one lifts resolution from 85% to 95%. Writing that specification is the hard part: an agent that must write its own gains nothing over an unaided baseline, and only 56% of those specifications pass our audit. The usual failure is faithfulness, a specification that constrains part of the required behavior and leaves the rest free. Specification quality still tracks the outcome, failing on 92% of unresolved instances against 51% of resolved ones, making faithful specification synthesis a concrete open problem.

title: IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation
abstract: Multi-task learning over heterogeneous data is fundamental to modern recommendation, while generative models are emerging as the backbone of next-generation recommenders. However, the integration of multi-task learning into the generative paradigm remains largely unexplored. Existing multi-task recommenders, in both discriminative and generative paradigms, extract task-relevant features from a single task-agnostic representation and wire tasks into a predefined conversion funnel. We show that this scheme is inherently prone to a threefold collapse. Source collapse, where task-specific signals are injected late and diluted in the shared latent space. Relational collapse, where task dependencies are either implicitly absorbed by the backbone or statically fixed by predefined funnels. Hierarchical collapse, where tasks depend on features at different scales and shift across training stages. We propose IntHQ, a multi-task generative recommender with three components, each alleviating one collapse. Dual-Stream Decoupling (DSD) injects task identity into computation stream early and separates the shared context stream from the task-specific stream, alleviating signal dilution. Task-Interactive Modeling (TIM) replaces the predefined funnel with explicit cross-task interaction, letting each task condition on the realized outcomes of its predecessors with learned, input-adaptive strength. Hierarchical Querying (HQ) lets each task gather multi-scale information across different layers at different training stages. In offline evaluations, IntHQ consistently outperforms competitive encoder backbones under four representative task-head configurations. Deployed in production on Amap, serving hundreds of millions of users for travel recommendation, IntHQ yields a 1.60\% relative UVCTR lift.

title: Disseny d’un sistema de cribratge mamogràfic basat en aprenentatge automàtic
abstract: [ES] Se diseña y evalúa un sistema de clasificación automatizada de mamografías basado en aprendizaje automático con el objetivo de contribuir a una detección más precisa y eficiente del cáncer de mama. El sistema opera a nivel de parche, clasificando regiones de interés en cinco categorías: tejido normal, masa benigna, calcificación benigna, masa maligna y calcificación maligna. A lo largo del trabajo se analiza el impacto de diferentes decisiones de diseño y se comparan las arquitecturas de ResNet50, Swin Transformer y NIKULIN, esta última especializada en imagen mamográfica. Finalmente, se explora la fusión de predicciones a nivel de parche para obtener una puntuación diagnóstica a nivel de mamografía completa, orientando así el sistema hacia un uso clínico real.
